basic_identification.full_title: Crosslinked Polyethylene Insulated Thermoplastic Sheathed Cables — Specification, Part 1: For Working Voltages up to and including 1 100 Volts (Second Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Electrotechnical / Power Cables (approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council and finalized by the Power Cables Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the physical, dimensional, and performance requirements for crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) insulated thermoplastic sheathed cables. These cables are designed for electric power transmission and distribution under working voltages up to and including 1 100 V a.c. or 1 500 V d.c. It covers single-core and multi-core configurations, including cables with improved fire performance (such as low halogen or halogen-free compounds).
scope.clause_number: Clause 1 (implied from title and Annex A)

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Electrical Cables (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Government of India, all Crosslinked Polyethylene Insulated Thermoplastic Sheathed Cables for working voltages up to 1 100 Volts must be certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards and bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, stocking, selling, or importing uncertified cables is a criminal offense. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial electrotechnical cables, as it is strictly reserved for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks.

requirements.detail: Every cable drum or attached label must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).
Conductors must be composed of plain copper or aluminium wires complying with IS 8130. For gassy mines, mining cables must feature copper conductors exclusively (tinned copper allowed on agreement).

The extruded cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) insulation must comply with strict physical-chemical limits: a) Tensile strength must be minimum 12.5 N/mm²; b) Elongation at break must be minimum 200 percent; c) After air oven aging (135 ± 3 °C for 7 days), maximum variation in tensile strength and elongation must not exceed ±25 percent; d) Hot set test (200 ± 3 °C, 15 min under 20 N/cm² load) must yield maximum elongation under load of 175% and maximum permanent elongation after cooling of 15%; e) Shrinkage test (130 ± 3 °C for 1 h) must not exceed 4.0%; f) Gravimetric water absorption (85 ± 2 °C for 14 days) must be maximum 1 mg/cm²; g) Volume resistivity must be minimum 1 x 10^14 ohm-cm at 27 °C and 1 x 10^12 ohm-cm at 90 °C.

The polyethylene (PE) sheathing compound must satisfy: a) Tensile strength min 12.5 N/mm² and elongation min 300% before aging; b) Air oven aging (110 ± 2 °C for 7 days) must yield minimum elongation of 300%; c) Hot deformation test (110 ± 2 °C for 6 h) must have a maximum indentation depth of 50 percent; d) Carbon black content for black sheaths must be 2.5 ± 0.5 percent.

Low Smoke Halogen Free (LSHF) sheathing (Type ST8 and ST12) must satisfy: a) Type ST8 tensile strength min 9.0 N/mm² and elongation min 125%; Type ST12 tensile strength min 12.5 N/mm² and elongation min 300%; b) Oven aging (ST8: 100 ± 2 °C for 7 days, max variation ±40%; ST12: 110 ± 2 °C for 10 days, max variation ±30%); c) Hot deformation (ST8: 80 ± 2 °C for 4 h, max indentation 50%; ST12: 110 ± 2 °C for 4 h, max indentation 50%); d) Cold elongation and cold impact test must show zero cracks and min 20% elongation at -15 ± 2 °C for 3 h; e) Shrinkage test (80 ± 2 °C for 5 h) must be maximum 3 percent.

requirements.requirement_type: Armour Coverage and Direction of Lay
requirements.detail: Armour must consist of galvanized round steel wires, formed steel wires (strips), or non-magnetic elements applied with a minimum coverage of 90 percent, calculated using the formula: Percent coverage = (N * d / W) * 100, where W = π * D * Cos α. The direction of lay of the armour must be left-hand.

Cables must be designated using standard letters: Aluminium conductor = A (no code letter for copper); XLPE insulation = 2X; Steel round wire armour = W; Non-magnetic round wire armour = Wa; Steel strip armour = F; Non-magnetic strip armour = Fa; Double steel strip armour = FF; Double steel round wire armour = WW; PVC outer sheath = Y; PE outer sheath = 2Y; LSHF outer sheath = Z.

Cables designed for fire-retardancy (Categories C1, C2, and C3) must satisfy: a) Flammability burning period must not exceed 60 s; b) Oxygen Index must be minimum 29; c) Temperature Index must be minimum 250 °C; d) Smoke density rating must be maximum 60 (FR-LSH) or 20 (LSHF); e) Halogen acid gas evolution (HCl) must be maximum 20% (FR-LSH) or 0.5% (LSHF); f) Light transmission for LSHF must be minimum 70 percent; g) Evolved gases must have a pH of minimum 4.3 and conductivity of maximum 10 µS/mm.

Drums must be selected randomly based on lot size: up to 25 drums (select 3, permissible defectives = 0); 26-50 (select 5, permissible defectives = 0); 51-100 (select 8, permissible defectives = 0); 101-300 (select 13, permissible defectives = 1); 301-500 (select 20, permissible defectives = 1); 501 and above (select 32, permissible defectives = 2). A drum sample is marked 'defective' if it fails any acceptance test.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 7098 (Part 1) : 2025 is the mandatory national Indian electrotechnical specification governing crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) insulated thermoplastic sheathed power cables for industrial and distribution systems operating at voltages up to 1 100 V. Under the national Power Cables Quality Control Order, all such cables sold or imported in India must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). The standard establishes strict physical and electrical limits for copper and aluminium conductors, XLPE insulation (including volume resistivity, thermal shrinkage, and hot-set deformation tests), and PVC, PE, or Low Smoke Halogen Free (LSHF) sheathing. It outlines a strict alphanumeric coding system to indicate material layouts (such as 'A2XWY' for armoured aluminium cables) and mandates rigorous fire, smoke, and halogen acid evolution limits for specialty fire-safe installations, ensuring robust safety and long-term transmission reliability.
